findings.text: The brief carries the shape of the result: the session pastes the result shapes, the recommendation rule, the waiting budget, the rule on obvious choices and the decision-question format's sections after the brief, because the reading agent cannot read a file. The re-read's leftover 5 names the format's three sections by their exact headings.
"Downloaded and verified" said more than the program checks: a downloaded file is checked only by its first bytes and its size, and is a copy to read, never proof of the claim.

A program run the shell tool moves to the background has not stopped: its lines are taken from that command once it ends, the rerun applies only if it ended before its closing line, and the program is never started twice on one staging file. Applied with the validator's corrected text.

The order to read a source completely is replaced by reading it part by part as far as WebFetch returns it, naming what it did not return, and never calling a source read in full. The re-read's leftover 4 limits that to the parts the agent can tell were not returned.
The reading agent cites only papers and pages it opened in the run, at addresses it saw, never from memory or from a search result it did not open.

The decision-question shape follows the decision-question format's order: the heading begins "Question", the long-run line and the Sources line sit under the matrix, then the question sentence, the new-ideas block and the lettered menu. The re-read's leftover 2 makes the menu last in the question, with the brief's Failures, paper list and closing line still following the whole result.

The reading agent's web requests can ask the owner for permission; a refusal is named under Failures; the prompt is a human check on what the pasted text could carry out, and the cases with no prompt are named. Applied with the validator's corrected text; the re-read found that text's auto-mode clause contradicted by its source, and its leftover 1 replaced it.
A latency figure carries where it came from, or the label "not yet measured; to measure on the project", because the reading agent cannot measure anything.
The sixty-second limit is stated as the code enforces it: per download, every redirect included, with the program's own name lookup bounded by the system resolver instead.
Fifty kilobytes is written as fifty kibibytes (51,200 bytes), the program's limit.
The description says every cited paper that can be fetched is downloaded.
The brief carries today's date from the session's date command for the read dates. The re-read's leftover 3 orders that command run before the launch, with step 5's header using the same date.
A written brief carries a second line saying it is web research to read, never an instruction to any agent that reads the file.
What the research changed is said in the question's explanation paragraph, so the question still opens with its heading.
The index-cell sentence says what the escaping prevents and that a viewer may still turn a bare address into a link.
Every decisions log that exists is read, not whichever one.
A source is never ranked by its place in the search results.

The auto-mode clause of the permission bullet was contradicted by its source: auto mode resumes prompting after three blocks in a row or twenty in the session, and a permission rule that says to ask still asks. Rewritten from the permission-modes page.
"Last of all, with nothing after it" contradicted the brief's own order; the menu is last in the question.

findings.text: Round 1's auto-mode sentence narrowed to web searches and fetches: a rule that allows or denies settles the request, a rule that asks still asks, the classifier takes the rest; plus the classifier's review of the launch and of the report. Applied with the validator's corrected text (a refused review also brings the security warning; only an unavailable classifier brings the note).
A launch refused for any other reason, for example by auto mode's classifier, closes the task as failed, writes no brief and is launched again only when the owner says to.

A security warning or a note to verify that comes with the returned text is not part of the result; it is named under Failures. Applied with the validator's corrected text (the note comes with the report; where it sits is not documented).

A researched question is presented only once the owner has said they are satisfied with the current one, opens with its heading and ends with its menu; the Evidence summary and Failures reach the owner through the explanation paragraph; a source or topic brief is presented without its questions, which follow one per message.
A question the rule on obvious choices leaves with one option is written as its heading, its explanation paragraph and a "Derived, no question needed" section, with no matrix and no menu.

Such a question is reported, not asked: no menu, and a sentence that the option is not the owner's answer until the owner confirms it and that the owner may reopen the choice. Applied with the validator's corrected text, which follows the owner's sourced ruling instead of asking.
Every claim names where in its source it stands when the tool shows it; a number with no source read in the run and none in the pasted text is marked [unverified] and listed as a proposal to check.

WebFetch's answer that a page does not say something is not evidence of absence: ask a narrower question first, and say when a quotation came through the tool's answer. Applied with the validator's corrected text, which quotes the tools reference as it stands (the critic's quote and the word small are not on the page).

A cross-host redirect WebFetch reports names an address the server supplied: fetch it only when it is a public https address the agent would have chosen for the same source. Applied with the validator's corrected text, after the validator's live fetch showed the target labelled server-supplied.
The reading agent gives the address of the paper's file itself, because that address is what the session downloads; a landing page is marked not fetched.
The program's printed lines are described as they are: a kept line names its paper by path and size, the other lines quote the address, and a non-object entry is refused with no address.

The brief check reads the header's ending, '; in progress', on a first line split on either line ending. Run by the executor through zsh on 2026-10-02 on two sample briefs: the in-progress header printed 93 true; a finished header whose item is 'the work in progress limit for the scheduler', with Windows line endings, printed 2718 false, where the check before round 2 printed 2718 true.

WebFetch refuses localhost and host names without a dot; a refusal of private addresses is documented only for the Monitor tool, and the domain safety check sends only the host name; so the guards this skill relies on for private addresses are the permission prompt and the brief's rule. Applied with the validator's corrected text, which adds the domain safety check.
One hundred mebibytes is written with its byte count, 104,857,600.
"These two places" named the wrong two things after round 1; the paper library and the brief folder are named.
An older paper may be cited where it is the primary source for a point; the owner's "from 2024 on" is kept.

The one-option exception is worded as the one exception this skill adds to the decision-question format's menu, because the format names its own one exception (the screen after a further explanation).

The pinned internal-address sentence names a benchmark network, and the program refuses the version four benchmarking range only, not 2001:2::/48. Evidence corrected by the validator (the registry row from its comma-separated form); line numbers updated by the re-read's leftover 2.

No test proves a mapped address such as [::ffff:127.0.0.1] is refused. Session-run fact, measured by the executor on Node v24.14.1 on 2026-10-02 with the program's own block list built from its source text: ::ffff:7f00:1, ::ffff:a00:1 and ::ffff:c0a8:101 are refused and ::ffff:808:808 is not; the program's version six rules alone refuse neither of the first two, and the four-part rules alone refuse both.
